title: Record that c=1 movers miss the 8-dimensional dihedral summand.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Exhaustive finite census for the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand inside the trivial-character `(+1,+1)` 216-space of the historical doubled centre block at `c=1`.

The `c=1` stabilizer has order 3072. Exactly 768 elements preserve that 216-space, and 2304 move it. For every mover `s`, the image of the summand `V` is orthogonal to `V`, and `s(V)` meets the 216-space only at zero. In particular no mover preserves `V`, and none preserves `V` while acting non-scalarly on it.

One explicit mover is the signed permutation whose coordinate map `k ↦ inv[k]` is `(0 3)(5 6)`, with every output sign positive. All eight basis images miss the 216-space, and they stay linearly independent modulo that space.

No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`.

Evidence class: exhaustive finite census of a finite set of order 3072, plus an exact rank computation over `Q` for each mover. The completeness argument is the decomposition of the hyperoctahedral group into 30 left cosets of the line-preserving subgroup. This is not a heuristic search and not an unrestricted nonexistence claim.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (priority revision 8).
- Assigned question: does any `c=1` stabilizer element that moves the 216-space preserve the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand and act non-scalarly on it?
- Predecessor: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7022
- Summand basis: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7023
- Finding being answered: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19514160
- Package: `research/c1-mover-8-summand/`

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. PR #7022 enumerated the stabilizer action on the 216-space and left this mover question open. Under the linear-character identification in PR #7008, elements that preserve the 216-space act by scalars on the summand; this census checks that prediction and then tests the movers. It does not redo the preserving-element census, the `A_1` characteristic polynomial of PR #7023, the different 8-dimensional joint space of PR #7019, or the 80-dimensional and 128-dimensional components.

The 768 preservers of the 216-space all preserve the summand and act by `±I`, 384 of each sign. That is a control. PR #7022 already places the outside-normalizer preservers among those 768 elements. This package does not recompute the normalizer.

Overlap on 2026-11-10 against `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`: local notes 10180, HEAD paths 10178, complete; 339 open PRs, pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T10:22:32Z; 7013 discussion records, pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T10:23:39Z. The phrases `8-dimensional dihedral`, `moves the 216`, and `isotypic summand` match #7008, #7022, #7023, and #7019. No open PR reports the action of a mover on this summand. Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, task metadata, and the ledger only. No code diffs.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only. Both modes passed. Metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Registered replay returned `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Selected baseline returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/c1-mover-8-summand/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/c1-mover-8-summand/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c1-mover-8-summand --check-only
```

Marker: `PASS_C1_MOVER_8_SUMMAND`.

The line-preserving signed-permutation group has order 344064 and index 30 in the hyperoctahedral group. The summand is the image of the multiplicity-8 projector for `ψ(r^k)=(-1)^k` and `ψ(r^k u)=(-1)^{k+1}`. Its Gram matrix is `48 I_8`. Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, the incomplete swap of coordinates 4 and 7, a swapped port label, a dropped projector support term, a repeated residual, and the PR #7022 witness, which is non-scalar on the 216-space and still acts by `-I` on the summand.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, any characteristic polynomial, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions. PR #6944 split the trivial `c=1` character into 216-dimensional blocks. PR #6964 pinned one 216-basis. PR #7008 computed the dihedral image and the multiplicity-8 character. PR #7022 enumerated the stabilizer on the 216-space and left the mover question open. PR #7023 built this summand's basis and proved reducibility under `A_1`. Ali Romman's PR #4958 and PR #4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Krzysztof Wojt's `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` supplies the 13 generators. The doubled representation comes from PR #1719. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

See `research/c1-mover-8-summand/TASK.json`.

- For the named mover `(0 3)(5 6)`, does `g` or `t` act by a scalar on the image of the summand? The image misses the `(+1,+1)` space. This is not the basis-transport question of PR #7019.
- Does any element of the line-preserving group outside the `c=1` stabilizer preserve this summand and act non-scalarly?
